claim: Verbal reports of the causes of choices and processes are often confabulated (Nisbett and Wilson), though how reliable introspection is in ordinary conditions remains unsettled. In a 94-study meta-analysis (Fox et al. 2011), plain concurrent think-aloud did not change performance on average (r about -0.03; one study found an exception for older adults on Raven's matrices), while explanation-style reports did.
agent_test: Compare accuracy of plain think-aloud vs explain-your-steps prompts at equal tokens on a reasoning set; measure change vs silent baseline.
note: Exact r=-0.03 still only from a search summary of Fox et al.; no LLM test of think-aloud vs explain found.
audit_note: Wikipedia says the evidence is arguably inadequate to decide how reliable introspection is and that Wilson conceded the 1977 claims went too far, and Fox and Charness found think-aloud raised older adults' Raven scores by about 11 IQ points, so 'unreliable' and 'does not change performance' are both stated more strongly than the sources; r=-.03 and 94 studies match Fox et al. 2011 abstract (seen via search result and Double and Birney).
claim_before_audit: Verbal reports of what caused a choice or process are unreliable (people confabulate), but concurrent plain think-aloud does not change performance (r about -0.03 over 94 studies); explanation-style reports do change it.

claim: LLM chain-of-thought is an unfaithful verbal report: models rarely mention hints or biases that drive their answers (reveal rate often under 20%; Claude 3.7 25%, R1 39% overall), and biased CoT cuts accuracy up to 36%.
schema_part: G (do not treat own rationale as evidence); O (verification by outside check)
agent_test: Inject hints into prompts; count how often the agent's trace mentions them; compare with an external-check operator.

claim: LLM introspection on internal states is narrow and fragile: self-prediction gain after finetuning (32.6 to 49.4%), about 20% injected-concept detection at best, and failure on language-knowledge introspection.
schema_part: none (background; do not rely on self-report of internal state)
agent_test: Ask agent to predict its own answer/confidence before answering; compare with a different model predicting it, at equal tokens.
note: Prompting-only self-access not shown (Song 21 models); injection detection is content-agnostic (Lederman and Mahowald).

claim: Randomised field trials of AI coding help give inconsistent productivity effects: +55.8% speed on a small greenfield task (N=95), +26% pull requests in pooled field trials (N=4,867), but +19% longer time for experienced developers on own repos (16 devs, 246 tasks).
agent_test: Run scaffold vs plain at equal tokens on both new-task and maintain-existing-code sets, report per-stratum effects.
note: METR 2026 round: returning devs 18% faster (CI -38% to +9%), new 4% (CI -15% to +9%); METR calls it very weak evidence and changed design because of selection effects.

claim: Developers and forecasters overestimate AI speedup and misjudge it afterwards (forecast 24%, post-hoc 20% faster, measured 19% slower; economists 39% and ML experts 38% faster predicted). Self-report is a poor outcome measure.
agent_test: Compare the agent's own estimate of gain from the scaffold vs measured gain.

claim: Programmers are overconfident judges of LLM output: they accept low-quality explanations with higher odds and confidence (OR 2.94; 3.99 vs 4.25 of 5).
agent_test: Test an LLM judge reviewing its own vs another model's output for accept-rate on seeded errors.

claim: Students are not a reliable stand-in for professionals: results differ in about half of values in TDD comparisons, and student vs professional gaps depend on site and task (Cliff's delta 0.37-0.47).
agent_test: Check that agent benchmark gains hold across difficulty strata, not just one population of tasks.

claim: TDD effect claims fail to replicate: the original 27% productivity gain disappeared in replications and task effects flipped direction.
agent_test: Replicate each scaffold gain on a fresh seed set and new tasks; flag sign flips.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM annotators can substitute for humans on easy, well-defined labelling tasks (model-model alpha 0.68-0.76; replace up to 50-60% by confidence selection) but fail on hard or subtle codes (causality human-model 0.22; security codes recall 0.47-0.73).
schema_part: O (use agreement between models as a check); memory none
agent_test: Use model-model agreement as an uncertainty trigger for the agent at equal tokens; compare with random selection.
audit_note: Minor: security-code recall 0.47-0.73 spans GPT-5 (0.47) to Qwen3-Max (0.73), and Camporese note the latter two models came close to human agreement, so the range is not uniformly a failure; Ahmed numbers (0.68-0.76, 0.22, up to 50-60% replaceable) match.

claim: LLM qualitative coding quality depends on prompt and codebook: one-shot gives most gain, few-shot may add nothing, definitions plus positive examples help, run-to-run SD small (0.02-0.04).
schema_part: O (prompt with definitions plus one example)
agent_test: Ablate zero/one/few-shot and definition-first prompts on a labelled set at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: run-to-run SD spans about 0.011 to 0.038 across models and prompts, slightly wider than 0.02-0.04.

claim: Agreement with humans is not the same as quality: human-LLM Jaccard 0.30 vs human-human 0.52, yet blind expert preferred LLM codes 48.5% vs 51.5% human.
agent_test: Judge outputs by blind expert/external verifier, not by agreement with a reference.

claim: LLM simulated participants match human averages on some classic tasks (r=0.95 moral scenarios; Ultimatum curve) but fail on reworded items and distributions; rich interview data raises accuracy to 72.8% vs 79.5% human retest.
schema_part: none (do not use LLM personas as evidence about humans)
agent_test: Test any persona-based critic on reworded versions of the same items; require stable results.

claim: Empirical SE studies using LLMs are poorly reproducible: of 18 with artifacts only 5 ran and none fully reproduced; pitfalls in all 72 papers; GPT-4 replications ran as-is in only 30% of modules.
agent_test: Log seeds, versions and temperature for every agent run; re-run a sample and report the spread.
note: Add: T=0 is not deterministic (18-44% of problems had no matching outputs across 5 samples); only 21.1% of 76 code-gen papers accounted for it; top-p moved pass rate about 12 points.
audit_note: Minor: the 72 papers were security and SE papers and the 18 were OpenAI-model papers with artifacts (Baltes cites Angermeir and Evertz secondhand); 30% is 7 of 23 modules.

claim: Observed behaviour differs from self-report in programmer studies: debugger use 43% self-reported vs 0 observed; METR cheating in 6% of disallowed recordings; screen recordings give a different slowdown (25%).
agent_test: Compare the agent's stated tool use with its actual call log.

claim: Experienced users do not improve quickly: up to 50 hours of Cursor use gave no clear speedup change; but heterogeneity by experience favours novices in Copilot trial.
agent_test: Measure scaffold effect by model strength tier.

claim: LLM judges of code have small, model-specific self-preference, but a larger problem: low agreement with test results (kappa 0.10 to 0.21 for GPT-4-turbo) and biases for length and position. Self-preference on verifiable tasks is mostly legitimate (own output really better); harmful cases persist when the judge erred as generator and shrink with long reasoning before the verdict.
schema_part: O (judge/verify operator: use tests or a different model)
agent_test: Have the agent judge its own vs another model's patches with test results hidden; compare to test outcome, controlling for length and position.

claim: Disagreement among repeated runs or sampled programs predicts error: code incoherence detects about 66-69% of erroneous tasks (16 LLMs, HumanEval and MBPP); agent action consistency gives 17.6 to 45.3 point accuracy gaps on HotpotQA. But it is weak for near-ceiling models and shared confident errors escape it (48% of high-agreement GPQA entries wrong).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare a disagreement-triggered verify step against always-verify and never-verify on coding tasks.

claim: METR retired its RCT design in Feb 2026: late-2025 round showed 18% (returning, CI -38 to +9) and 4% (new, CI -15 to +9) speedups, both with CIs including zero, with selection effects (task withholding by 30-50% of developers, pay cut, timing problems). The sign gap to earlier gains is not cleanly explained.
schema_part: G (do not trust headline productivity numbers)
agent_test: None; background for how to measure agent gains.

claim: No coding-agent-specific trace faithfulness number, no LLM think-aloud vs explain reactivity test, no prompting-only Binder replication on frontier models, and no LLM-participant replication of TDD or student-vs-professional results were found.
agent_test: Run our own: silent vs narrate vs explain at equal tokens; hint injection in SWE-style tasks counting hint mentions vs hint-driven edits.
